correctness.rationale: The source proves that \(n\in\mathfrak S_\mu\) iff \(\mu/n+\sum_{p\mid n}1/p\) is an integer. Under \(\mu>0\) and \(n>\mu\), each of the three shapes with \(\Omega(n)\le2\) makes that positive integer strictly less than \(2\), so it must equal \(1\). This yields exactly \(\mu=p-1\), \(\mu=p(p-1)\), or \(\mu=pq-p-q\), and substitution proves every converse. The \(\mu=673\) corollary follows by exhaustive factor-pair and discriminant checks.

value.rationale: The classification is tied directly to the source's open Conjecture 1(ii), not to an arbitrary cutoff. It completely removes all prime, prime-square, and squarefree-semiprime candidates from the unresolved search and turns the source's hardest reported positive parameter \(\mu=673\) from a bounded computational failure into an unbounded structural statement: any future witness must have \(\Omega(n)\ge3\). This is a natural low-complexity boundary that can guide further search and theory.
